label: First trip to Russian State
description: Jenkinson's first journey to the Russian State and Central Asia.

sources.quote: ...he was on Russian lands from July 12, 1557 to August 10, 1558...

label: Return from Central Asia
description: Jenkinson's return journey from Central Asia through Russia.

sources.quote: ...again, on his way back from Central Asia, from May 28, 1559 to May 9, 1560.

label: Map published in London
description: Jenkinson's map published with the date 1562.

sources.quote: This article examines the map called "Nova absolutaque Russiae, Moscoviae, et Tartariae descriptio " published in London in 1562 the author of which was a famous trader, diplomat and Queen Elizabeth I Tudor̓ s official ambassador to the Safavid Empire Anthony Jenkinson.

label: Mission to Safavid Empire starts
description: Jenkinson sent on behalf of Queen Elizabeth I to the Russian and Safavid States.

sources.quote: It should be noted that from May 14, 1561 to September 28, 1564, having gone on behalf of Queen Elizabeth I to the Russian and Safavid States as an ambassador of the English crown and a trade representative of the Moscow company, Jenkinson was not in London, where the map was published.

label: Met Safavid envoy
description: Jenkinson dined with Safavid envoy in presence of Tsar Ivan the Terrible.

sources.quote: ...he not only dined in the presence of Tsar Ivan the Terrible on March 15, 1562, but also set off with him on his way to the Safavid Empire...

label: Departed for Safavid Empire
description: Jenkinson left Russian State for Safavid Empire.

sources.quote: Accordingly, Anthony met the year 1562 in the Russian State, from where on April 27, 1562 he went further to the Safavid Empire, staying there until the spring of 1563.

label: Received in Shamakhi
description: Jenkinson received by ruler of Shirvan, Abdalla Khan.

sources.quote: On August 20, 1562, in Shamakhi, Anthony was received by the ruler of Shirvan, Abdalla Khan, whom Jenkinson describes as follows: "…richly dressed in long silk and brocade clothes…"

label: Met Shah Tahmasib I
description: Jenkinson's audience with Shah Tahmasib I in Qazvin.

sources.quote: Although the long -awaited for the British audience of Anthony Jenkinson with Shah Tahmasib I, which took place on November 20, 1562 in Qazvin, ended not so fruitfully...

label: Returned to London
description: Jenkinson returned to London after his mission.

sources.quote: Anthony indicates the exact date of his return to London, namely September 28, 1564, it can be assumed that this " Declaration" was compiled by Jenkinson either in the autumn-winter of 1564, immediately upon his return (at best!), or already in 1565.

label: Ortelius atlas published
description: Theatrum Orbis Terranum published including Jenkinson's map.

sources.quote: It was an integral part of the world's first modern geographical atlas "Theatrum Orbis Terranum" ("Theatre of the Orb of the World "), published in 1570 as a result of the p ainstaking work of the famous Flemish cartographer and geographer of the 16th century Abraham Ortelius.

label: Mercator world map reissued
description: Mercator reissued his world map using Jenkinson's map.

sources.quote: Jenkinson's map, in addition to Ortelius, was also used by the famous and greatest Flemish cartographer and geographer Gerardus Mercator when reissuing in 1572 his famous map of the world...

label: Original map discovered
description: Krystina Szykula discovered the original Jenkinson map.

sources.quote: 1987 was remembered for K. Szykula's sensational statement: a genuine copy of Jenkinson's map was discovered!

label: Map discovery announced
description: Szykula announced the discovery at International Conference on the History of Cartography.

sources.quote: In 1989, sensational news spread around the scientific world: at the regular XIII International Conference on the History of Cartography held in Amsterdam, the Polish cartographer Krystina Szykula... announced the discovery of the original Jenkinson map of 1562.
